uncited: This family encompasses methods that generate structured 3D volumes from non-volumetric sources (such as point clouds, meshes, or image sets) for the purpose of rendering or analysis.
It solves the problem of converting continuous or sparse representations into discrete voxel grids with semantic or photometric labels.

It is distinguished from sibling methods like [Voxelization](12-voxelization.md) by focusing on the semantic assignment (segmentation) or photometric consistency (coloring) of the volume content rather than simple geometric occupancy.
The method was developed to address the limitations of earlier volumetric reconstruction techniques that struggled with texture consistency and visibility.
It has been widely used in computer vision for 3D modeling from image sequences.
